newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut Blue Cross agrees to merge with Anthem.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut Blue Cross agrees to merge with Anthem.

text.p: Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut said Tuesday its board of directors had agreed in principle to merge with Indianapolis-based Anthem Inc, forming a multi-regional company with more than $11.5 billion in revenues.
The proposal to merge the two mutual insurance companies awaits the approval of the Anthem board later this week, Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut said.
Insurance commissioners in Connecticut and Indiana, as well as the policyholders of both companies, must approve the merger.
The merger is scheduled to be finalized in 1997, the Connecticut Blue Cross said. As part of the merger, it will be given two seats on the Anthem board of directors.
The Connecticut Blue would become part of Anthem East Inc, based in Newark, which will serve as the center of operations for Anthem on the East Coast.

Anthem East also will administer Blue Cross & Blue Shield of New Jersey, which Anthem agreed to acquire earlier this year. Blue Cross and Blue Shield of New Jersey, meanwhile, had previously agreed to acquire the assets of Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Delaware.
The Blue Cross & Blue Shield of New Jersey deal is expected to be completed in early 1997, an Anthem spokesman said.
The Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut merger does not involve cash payments.

"This is an exciting opportunity for Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut and undoubtedly, the most dramatic change proposed since the company was founded more than 60 years ago," said chairman and chief executive John Croweak.

"It is critical that we seize this opportunity if we are to become bigger, stronger, more competitive and better positioned to survive in the rapidly changing world that is health care today," he said.
Just last week, Empire Blue Cross & Blue Shield announced plans to convert to a for-profit corporation to better compete with the managed care market.
Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut is Connecticut's leading and largest managed care company, providing health care benefits and managed care programs to about 850,000 Connecticut residents.
In 1995, Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut had revenues of $1.5 billion.
Anthem Inc, the parent of insurance broker Acordia Inc, covers more than nine million people nationwide and had consolidated revenues in 1995 of $7.5 billion.
Blue Cross & Blue Shield of Connecticut said the proposed merger will have little impact on its members, customers, providers and employees at this time.
The Connecticut Blue said it had no immediate or specific plans to make changes to its work force of about 2,300 employees.

When the pending mergers with the New Jersey and Connecticut Blues are completed, Anthem will rank among the top five health care management companies in the United States, with consolidated revenues of more than $11.5 billion. Combined assets will equal more than $7.5 billion and policyholders' equity will be more than $1.8 billion.
